resale_co.name: Certificate of Occupancy (resale / change of ownership), Borough Code Chapter 117 Article II
resale_co.issued_by: Borough of Pemberton Code Enforcement Official (Department of Inspections)
resale_co.lead_time: By ordinance the certificate is granted or denied within 10 business days of the application.
requirements: Home and premises must comply with the current International Property Maintenance Code and the Borough's health, sanitation, maintenance and occupancy ordinances

fees.label: Initial resale CO inspection (application form, created November 2024)

resale_co.how_to_apply: Download the Re-Sale Inspection Form (Certificate of Occupancy Inspection Application, a Word file) from the Borough Forms page, fill in block, lot, location, owner and buyer, and submit it with the fee to the Department of Inspections, Borough Hall, 50 Egbert St., Pemberton, NJ 08068. The office-use box lists check, cash or credit card. The fee is nonrefundable and is paid when the application is filed. Call the Borough at 609-894-8222.

evidence.quote: BOROUGH OF PEMBERTON Department of Inspections 50 Egbert St. Pemberton, NJ 08068 CERTIFICATE OF OCCUPANCY INSPECTION APPLICATION

shall sell, transfer, assign, or grant the title or change in ownership of any home, dwelling, apartment, cooperative or condominium unit which is used or intended to be used for human occupancy until and unless a certificate of occupancy

The certificate of occupancy shall first be obtained from the Code Enforcement Official, which certificate of occupancy shall be granted or denied within 10 business days from the date of application for the same.

A nonrefundable fee, the amount of which shall be set by resolution, to cover the cost of initial inspection requirements in connection with such application shall be paid to Pemberton Borough at the time the application is filed.
The certificate of occupancy shall be good for 60 days.
ph: 609-894-8222 50 Egbert Street Pemberton, New Jersey 08068

resale_co.notes: Borough Code Chapter 117, Article II (Ord. No. 2003-2, fees amended by Ord. No. 2024-9 on November 18, 2024; code current through 12-15-2025) bars any sale or change in ownership of a home until a certificate of occupancy is issued by the Code Enforcement Official; it was read in full through the ecode360 print view. The ordinance leaves the fee amounts to a council resolution, which was not found online; the $100 initial and $75 re-inspection amounts come from the Borough's application form (Word file created November 19, 2024, the same month as Ord. No. 2024-9). The form is a .docx file, so an automatic text check may not read it. No inspector name, email or checklist is published. The Forms page also has a Rental Inspection Certificate, Landlord Rental Registration and Vacant and Abandoned Registration Form (not resale requirements).

requirements: Smoke alarms and carbon monoxide alarms as required by N.J.A.C. 5:70-4.19 (state certificate, now called the Certificate of Smoke Alarm, Carbon Monoxide Alarm, and Secondary Power Source Identification Label Compliance); homes with a generator, solar or battery storage need the power source label

authorities.name: NJ DCA Division of Fire Safety, Bureau of Fire Code Enforcement (State is the fire code enforcing agency for Pemberton Borough)
authorities.lead_time: Apply more than 10 business days before the closing date for the lowest fee.

authorities.how_to_apply: Apply online through the NJ DCA Division of Fire Safety smoke certificate application (Fire Solutions portal). Pay by e-check or credit card when applying; the certificate is emailed once the fee is paid and any required inspection is done. Questions: Bureau of Fire Code Enforcement, (609) 633-6106.

fire_cert.notes: Pemberton Borough has no local fire enforcing agency: the DCA LEA registry (July 2026) lists it as S (State), the DCA state towns list (July 17, 2026) marks it SC (the state issues smoke certificates), and the Borough's own Fire Prevention chapter (Chapter 102) has its enforcement articles repealed (Ord. No. 2010-10). State fees are $45 / $90 / $161 by business days before the change of occupant (N.J.A.C. 5:70-2.9(d)). The Good Will Fire Company (200 Hanover Street, 609-894-2168) is the fire company and does not issue resale certificates. The state directory (survey 8/17/2026) lists Louis Kilmer, (609) 633-6132, PO Box 809, Trenton, as the fire official; the BFCE office page lists (609) 633-6106.
